events.title: Telegram
events.text:
⚡️ News Roundup: There are so many things going on simultaneously right now that it is genuinely overwhelming. I felt the need to zoom out for a second and take inventory:
1. The Ansarallah offensive against the Saudi mercenaries in Yemen continues. They are striking Saudi oil infrastructure and airports with drones/missiles. Ansarallah are currently winning the armed struggle on the ground and are poised to capture the city of Taiz.
2. IDF West Bank incursions in response to the resistance operation that killed two Israeli soldiers. They are engaging in destruction operations against civilians in Southern Lebanon. They are also killing people in Gaza every day.
3. Riots and protests taking place across Europe: Belgium, France, Denmark, Spain, Italy, Albania, Serbia, Greece, Portugal, etc. The main grievance is the rising cost of living because of increased petrol prices. Similar unrest is taking place in South America.
4. Upcoming US/Israeli escalations against Iran, which is going to make crude oil even more expensive with the usual downstream effects.
5. The Israelis appear to be establishing foothold in Syria through the Druze, which they are using as proxies. Keep an eye on that.
6. The US midterm elections on November 3rd. Republicans could lose control of Congress to the Democrats, whose constituents are now strongly anti-war.
7. The Israeli elections are on October 27th. Netanyahu could lose power to Eisenkot. It is unclear what, if anything, will change if Eisenkot takes over.
8. Continuous warfare at various levels of intensity in Sudan, Ukraine, Congo, Sahel Region, Afghanistan/Pakistan, Columbia, Myanmar.
9. China is doing nothing and it’s going great for them.
10. (Insert thing I forgot to mention)
The world is a complex system, but all of these conflicts are interconnected. I could point to any item on this list and see how it directly (or indirectly) connects to the others. It’s fascinating.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇺🇸 US loads up for possible strike against Iran - report
The USS George Washington strike group in the Arabian Sea has been loading large deliveries of standoff land-attack missiles and bunker-buster bombs designed to penetrate fortified underground targets, the Wall St. Journal reports. 
The preparations follow reports that US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for a shorter but more intense campaign on Iran after the November midterms, potentially targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear sites, and missile and drone arsenals.
Meanwhile, the State Department has begun [drawing down personnel at four embassies](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76702) in the region — Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar, and the UAE — citing an elevated threat environment. Non-essential staff and families were ordered out of Saudi Arabia earlier in the week.
👉 The pattern is consistent with preparation for a worst-case scenario. Embassies are thinning their footprints to reduce exposure if retaliation comes, while the military positions the munitions it would need if the attack order is given.
Iran has previously warned that any renewed US or Israeli strikes would trigger [retaliation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76599) against American bases, warships, and Gulf infrastructure, and has reportedly drawn up [plans](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76684) to target undersea communications cables.

events.text:
📹 Houthis launch ample attack across Saudi Arabia
Houthi forces have carried out seven missile and drone operations deep inside Saudi territory in retaliation for a Saudi air campaign against civilian targets, the movement's spokesman Brigadier General Yahya Saree stated.
Targets hit:
🌏  King Khalid Airport in Riyadh
🌏 Aramco facilities in Yanbu
🌏 The Rabigh oil refinery
🌏 Oil pumping stations and the East-West pipeline
🌏 King Fahd International Airport in Dammam
🌏 Najran International Airport
The Ansar Allah movement has vowed to keep hitting targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, framing the campaign as "escalation for escalation" until the Saudi aggression stops and the blockade on Yemen is lifted.
